SSP pipes with ≥100K requests in this scope (top 10 by volume). A pipe carrying exactly one DSP over the window (Direct or BidSwitch), with no unattributed traffic, is shown as that DSP and can drill into brands. Reseller pools fan requests out inside the reseller's exchange — that step is not observable from Seedtag data, so the SSP is the last level. Pipes marked 1 DSP + unmapped carry one named seat alongside traffic the demand table cannot attribute; naming the whole pipe after that seat would overstate it, so they stop here too.

Top 10 advertiser domains by bids for this DSP in this demand scope, same window. Only bids that actually happened appear — a brand not bidding leaves no trace.

Source: SSP events daily — all products, user-country grain, Jul 15 – Aug 13, 2026. Inactivity definition: bid rate < 0.80% with ≥1M requests over the window. Watchlist countries (TR, SG, HK) are pinned to the list regardless of bid rate and flagged as such. Editorial-group detail: top 15 per country, ≥100K requests. Demand drill: SSP pipes from the same events table; DSP identity and brands from the enriched demand responses table (Beachfront excluded). Reference points (active markets, same window): ES 2.26%, DE 2.19%, GB 2.12%, US 0.91%, FR 0.75%.

Money columns are operational figures in USD from the event stream: Revenue = Seedtag revenue (net paid − post-auction discounts + curator margin); Pub cost = an SSP-side allocation estimate (impression cost + HB net insert cost); Margin = (Revenue − Pub cost) / Revenue. These are the only revenue/cost figures that exist at user-country grain — they do not reconcile with Finance's Publisher Revenue (publisher-reported, EUR, monthly-average FX, publisher grain only). True publisher payout is defined per publisher, never per user country, so splitting it by the viewer's country is a proxy: read Pub cost and Margin as directional only. The Brands view shows revenue from the enriched demand table, a slightly different adjustment basis.
